item.text:
**Verdict:** Mixed, leaning slightly positive on technocratic pockets rather than broad, systemwide service-delivery reform. The strongest positive evidence is Turkey’s centralized, digitized health procurement at DMO; the clearest negative evidence is opaque, politically fraught reconstruction in Hatay and a tightly controlled information environment that weakens transparent correction. I found little direct 2024 evidence on education, disability services, or ministry-wide public dashboards/audit loops beyond procurement.

| Side | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| Positive | Great Savings in Public Medical Supplies and Pharmaceuticals Procurement | Devlet Malzeme Ofisi Genel Müdürlüğü | 2024-10-17 | https://www.dmo.gov.tr/Home/Icerik/3992 | DMO says its Health Market bulk-procurement system expanded to 10,000 medical supplies and 3,000 drugs, covered 62% of Ministry of Health/university-hospital supply needs and 93% of pharmaceuticals, logged large savings in 2024, and relied on centralized e-tenders, technical suitability checks, and digitalized procurement. This is the cleanest evidence of measurement-driven service delivery. | 6B.5; 6B.4 |
| Positive | Foreword by Director General | Devlet Malzeme Ofisi Genel Müdürlüğü | 2024-05-03 | https://www.dmo.gov.tr/Eng/Home/EngIcerik/1212 | DMO describes itself as a central purchasing body using a professional, innovative approach, stressing transparency, competition, accountability, lawful and efficient use of public resources, and fast digital e-tenders for hospitals. This supports a technocratic, not patronage-based, model of social-service procurement. | 6B.5; 6B.4 |
| Positive | Turkiye: 2024 Article IV Mission Press Release | IMF | 2024-08-28 | https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/08/28/pr24311-turkiye-2024-article-iv-mission-press-release | IMF says the policy turnaround since mid-2023 tightened the macro mix, sharply reduced crisis risks, and raised confidence. This is indirect but real evidence of data-driven correction, though it is macro policy rather than a direct social-service delivery case. | 6B.5; 5B.9 |
| Positive | Turkey completes new homes in area hit by devastating earthquake | Reuters | 2024-02-03 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/turkey-completes-new-homes-in-area-hit-by-devastating-earthquake-3291916 | Reuters reports the government handed over 7,275 homes in Hatay and framed reconstruction with explicit targets, tender counts, and registration data for families. This is weaker than the DMO evidence, but it does show measured output tracking in disaster-housing delivery. | 6B.5; 6B.2 |
| Negative | Shock and confusion as Turkey seizes earthquake survivors' homes | Reuters | 2024-03-18 | https://www.reuters.com/commodities/shock-confusion-as-turkey-seizes-earthquake-survivors-homes-2024-03-18/ | Reuters found thousands of Hatay homeowners blindsided by Treasury seizures under an urban-transformation amendment, with unclear compensation and unanswered questions from the government. That points to opaque correction, weak communication, and politically fraught service delivery. | 6B.5; 6B.2 |
| Negative | Turkey | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/turkey | The report says Erdoğan entered the term with continued tight media control, and incumbents benefited from disproportionate airtime. That weakens the transparency and feedback environment needed for evidence-based correction in public services. | 6B.5; 5B.6 |

**Search gap:** I did not find strong direct 2024 evidence showing the health, education, disability, or social-protection ministries themselves using public metrics, audits, or published corrective dashboards to improve service delivery. The best direct evidence is concentrated in DMO health procurement; the main counterevidence is reconstruction opacity and broader information control.
